title: Find the longest common subsequence
prompt: A subsequence of a string is what is left after deleting any of its characters, without reordering the rest. Return the length of the longest subsequence that a and b have in common. For "abcde" and "ace" it is 3, from "ace". The characters need not be next to each other.
hints: Let one entry mean: the answer for the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b. What is it when either count is 0?
Look at the last character of each prefix. If they are equal, that character extends the answer for both prefixes one shorter.
If a[i - 1] equals b[j - 1], the entry is table[i - 1][j - 1] + 1. Otherwise it is the larger of table[i - 1][j] and table[i][j - 1].
checkLabels: Strings with no character in common give 0.
The shared characters must be in the same order in both.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Finds the longest run of characters that are next to each other in both strings.
Counts characters of b that appear anywhere in a, ignoring their order.

feedback: Fill the table by hand for "abc" and "ac". Each entry depends on the entry up and to the left, the one above, and the one to the left.
